narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the company has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. First, your overall years of experience had the strongest influence, pulling the decision toward staying. With only 1-5 years of total experience, you are in the most common group among employees the model expects to remain, yet this shorter track record still weighed noticeably against a long-term commitment signal.

The second strongest factor was that you have received other job offers while at the company. This pushed the prediction toward leaving, as outside opportunities often signal that an employee is considering alternatives.

Third, the length of time you have spent in your current role also nudged the outcome toward leaving. Like your total experience, your 1-5 years here places you in the largest group of stayers, but the model interpreted the relatively short tenure as increasing the likelihood of departure.

Taken together, these elements created a slight tilt toward predicting that you will leave. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly, explore whether the external offers reflect unmet needs, and consider how additional experience or clearer growth paths might change your outlook. You may want to reflect on what would make staying feel more secure and rewarding.
